notes:
Promptline says so when Ctrl+Alt+V is how your keyboard layout types a character, the update check's TLS library and the app framework carry their security patches, and the pack survey no longer names a private tool. Builds on [v0.2.25](https://github.com/bekalpaslan/promptline/releases/tag/v0.2.25).

### Hotkey

- **A notice when the hotkey is a character on your layout.** Windows treats the right Alt key as Ctrl+Alt on layouts that have AltGr, so a Ctrl+Alt+V hotkey also fires on AltGr+V and swallows what that key would type. On the Czech, Slovak, Hungarian, Croatian and Slovenian layouts that is `@`. From this release, when a registered hotkey is such a combination on any layout installed on the machine, the manager shows a persistent notice naming the layout and the character ("On your Czech keyboard layout, Ctrl+Alt+V is how you type @, and Promptline takes it while it runs") and points at Settings → Global hotkey. Close it and it stays closed for that combination; change the hotkey or the layouts and it is checked again. The default stays Ctrl+Alt+V: every alternative loses something too (Ctrl+Shift+V is paste in Windows Terminal and browsers).
- Settings' hotkey help names the default's known collisions: the AltGr `@` above and *Introduce Variable* in JetBrains' Windows keymap, which a system-wide Ctrl+Alt+V takes from IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm and Rider.

### Generate

- The survey the Generate dialog puts on the clipboard, the hint under an empty topic and the pack template no longer give a private planning tool's command as the example of a workflow command to wrap. The example is generic now: any slash commands or skills the project defines.

### Under the hood

- **The update check's TLS library was patched.** The daily check for a new version is still the app's one network request, to `promptline.cc/latest.json`, and it sends nothing new; the library that makes the connection (rustls 0.23.46, rustls-webpki 0.103.16) carries its latest fixes.
- **The app framework carries its security fix.** Tauri 2.11.6 closes an advisory in which a web page loaded inside an app could read another window's responses. Promptline loads no web pages, only its own two windows, so nothing could reach it; the patch is taken all the same, and nothing changes.
- A first run's Starter pack is read from the same file the repository ships as `packs/starter.json`, so the two can't drift. An existing library is not touched.

Nothing on disk changes, and the app sends nothing new over the network.
